nindian-society-4-3.s: A caste that is economically and politically powerful is called a:
nindian-society-4-3.x: A dominant caste is one with economic and political power; Sanskritisation, by contrast, is the copying of upper-caste practices.

nindian-society-17-9.s: Caste status, a fixed social position, is closely linked with:
nindian-society-17-9.x: Caste status is tied to occupation and fixed by birth, not obtained through personal effort.

nindian-society-17-15.s: Which of the following is an example of achieved status?
nindian-society-17-15.x: IAS officer, doctor and scientist are achieved statuses; caste, gender and family background are ascribed.

n68b35218354.s: Who defined caste as a system in which, at least ideally, there is no mobility up or down the status ladder?
n68b35218354.x: A. W. Green defined caste as a system of stratification in which status mobility, at least ideally, may not occur.

nindian-society-5-4.s: Which of the following is a modern basis of social stratification in India?
nindian-society-5-4.x: Political power and urbanisation are modern bases; caste, varna and tribe are traditional bases.

nindian-society-19-18.s: Which of the following has weakened hereditary occupations in India?
nindian-society-19-18.x: Education, industrialisation, urbanisation and occupational mobility have weakened hereditary occupations.

nd09e507c9d3.s: In recent times, inter-caste conflicts in India are mostly about:
nd09e507c9d3.x: Inter-caste conflicts are now mostly about power rather than ritual status, and caste dominance rests increasingly on secular factors (no dates, so not a sequence).

n63ad7b4bd16.s: How many indicators did the Mandal Commission use to identify OBCs?
n63ad7b4bd16.x: The Mandal Commission used 11 indicators (4 social, 4 economic, 3 educational) and put OBCs at over 52 per cent of the population.

nc854f4610e8.s: Dalit social change has come through state policy, reform movements and:
nc854f4610e8.x: The three avenues of Dalit change are state policy, reform movements, and Sanskritisation or Westernisation.

nb5c48a0de1b.s: The line between village and town begins to be crossed with the emergence of:
nb5c48a0de1b.x: Traders and manufacturers, not wholly dependent on village resources, mark the start of the village-to-town transition.

nac7c7a87adc.s: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of urban life?
nac7c7a87adc.x: Urban life is marked by competition, impersonal relations, anonymity and weak control; informal ties and face-to-face relations are village traits.

ndfcd638f751.s: According to Louis Wirth, urbanism is produced by size, density and:
ndfcd638f751.x: Wirth ('Urbanism as a Way of Life', 1938) named size, density and heterogeneity; homogeneity is a village trait.

n5e5528f426c.s: In Redfield and Singer's typology, primary urbanisation is:
n5e5528f426c.x: Primary urbanisation is orthogenetic (cities of moral order, temple centres); secondary urbanisation is heterogenetic.

nf6b0464f167.s: Urban wages in India are about how many times rural wages?
nf6b0464f167.x: Urban wages are about 1.7-2 times rural wages, a pull factor alongside push factors like monsoon failure and rural unemployment.

n32f1b043864.s: Which one of the following districts was NOT less urbanised in 2011 than India was in 1991 (22.87%)?
n32f1b043864.x: Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and West Godavari were below 22.87%; Visakhapatnam (47.45%) was the most urbanised district.

n8f7bc60f5d2.s: About what share of Indian marriages are inter-caste?
n8f7bc60f5d2.x: Only about 5% of Indian marriages are inter-caste, as endogamy keeps caste boundaries and 'purity' intact.

n83e842056f3.s: Migrants carrying caste prejudice into cities and caste networks deciding informal jobs illustrate:
n83e842056f3.x: Urban anonymity has limits: caste networks, caste associations and caste stickers persist, so caste identity does not disappear in cities.

nc7581a1e9a9.s: The Aruvippuram Shiva consecration of 1888 was performed by:
nc7581a1e9a9.x: Sree Narayana Guru performed the Aruvippuram consecration (1888) and gave 'One Caste, One Religion, One God'; the Self-Respect Movement (1925) was Periyar's.

n7a1fd8546ed.s: In which year did the Justice Party win the Communal G.O.?
n7a1fd8546ed.x: The Communal G.O. was won in 1921; 1909 is the year of the Minto-Morley Reforms.

n08b20344028.s: In which year did the Supreme Court, in Lata Singh v. State of UP, hold there is no bar on inter-caste marriage?
n08b20344028.x: Lata Singh v. State of UP (2006) held there is no bar on inter-caste marriage and directed police to protect such couples.

new.s: The conflict theory of stratification, based on ownership of the means of production, is associated with:
new.x: Marx linked class to ownership of the means of production and class struggle.

new.s: Davis and Moore put forward the functionalist theory of stratification in:
new.x: Davis and Moore (1945) argued that unequal rewards pull scarce talent into key posts.

new.s: Tumin's description of stratification as 'consequential' means that it:
new.x: For Tumin, stratification is consequential because it decides life chances; 'universal' and 'ancient' are separate features.

new.s: The real, local birth groups of the caste system, as distinct from the four-fold theoretical order, are called:
new.x: Varna is the four-fold theoretical scheme; jatis are the real, local birth groups ranked by ritual purity.

new.s: Sorokin's 'Social Mobility', which first set out vertical and horizontal mobility, was published in:
new.x: Pitirim Sorokin's 'Social Mobility' (1927) first systematically distinguished vertical and horizontal mobility.

new.s: A labourer's son becoming an engineer is an example of:
new.x: Inter-generational mobility is a change of position between parents and children.

new.s: Mobility caused by a change in the occupational structure itself is called:
new.x: Structural mobility results from a change in the occupational structure of society.

new.s: In Daniel Thorner's scheme, landlords who live on rent are called:
new.x: Thorner's Maliks live on rent; Kisans own land and use family labour; Mazdoors are tenants, sharecroppers and landless labourers.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (Thorner's class – description) is correctly matched?
o: Kisans – own land, work with family labour
new.x: Kisans own land and use family labour; Maliks are rent-receiving landlords and Mazdoors are tenants, sharecroppers and the landless.

new.s: In his Sripuram study, Andre Beteille found that caste, class and power:
new.x: Beteille's 'Caste, Class and Power' (1965) showed that caste, class and power diverge in Sripuram, Thanjavur.

new.s: The English-educated middle class that arose after Macaulay's Minute (1835) was analysed in 'Social Background of Indian Nationalism' by:
new.x: A.R. Desai traced the English-educated middle class to Macaulay's Minute of 1835.

new.s: According to the OECD, India will have the world's largest middle class by:
new.x: The OECD projects India's middle class to be the world's largest by 2035; 2047 is the year it is projected to reach 61%.

new.s: The Telangana caste survey found how many castes above average backwardness?
new.x: Of 242 castes ranked, 135 (67%) were above average backwardness.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT listed by the Economic Survey 2025-26 as a driver of social mobility?
new.x: The ES 2025-26 names health, education, technology and institutions as drivers of mobility; land inheritance is not one.

new.s: The concept of status inconsistency, holding different ranks on different dimensions, is associated with:
new.x: Lenski's status inconsistency means a person ranks differently on different dimensions of stratification.

new.s: In Weber's analysis, a person's access to necessities and opportunities is called:
new.x: Weber's life chances are access to necessities and opportunities, decided by market situation.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the status group:
1. The concept is Max Weber's.
2. Its members share a common lifestyle.
3. Caste is an open status group.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Weber's status group shares a lifestyle; statement 3 is wrong because caste is a closed status group.

new.s: Shamirpet, near Hyderabad, was studied by:
new.x: S.C. Dube studied Shamirpet in 'Indian Village' (1955); Srinivas studied Rampura.

new.s: 'The Remembered Village', on Rampura in Mysore, was written by:
new.x: M.N. Srinivas wrote 'The Remembered Village' on Rampura.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (village – scholar) is correctly matched?
new.x: Kishan Garhi was Marriott's village; Rampura is Srinivas's, Shamirpet Dube's and Sripuram Beteille's.

new.s: Redfield developed the folk-urban continuum from his study of:
new.x: Redfield's folk-urban continuum came from Yucatan in Mexico and sees settlements on a gradual scale.

new.s: In a village, as against a town, social control is mainly:
new.x: Villages rely on informal control by caste and custom; towns on formal control by law and police.

new.s: A census town needs at least what share of male main workers in non-farm work?
new.x: The census town criteria are 5,000 people, 75% (not 60%) male workers in non-farm work and 400 persons per sq km.

new.s: As per Census 2011, what share of India's population was rural?
new.x: In 2011, 68.8% of India was rural and 31.16% urban.

new.s: The typology of primary and secondary urbanisation was given by:
new.x: Robert Redfield and Milton Singer gave the primary (orthogenetic) and secondary (heterogenetic) typology.

new.s: Secondary (heterogenetic) urbanisation is marked by:
o: Folk culture growing into a Great Tradition
new.x: Heterogenetic change replaces old thought with new; folk culture growing into the Great Tradition is primary urbanisation.

new.s: The main driver of urbanisation, whose density is linked to rising crime, is:
new.x: Industrialisation drives urbanisation, and the resulting density raises crime.

new.s: As per the Economic Survey 2025-26, what share of rural households lack healthcare within 5 km?
new.x: The ES 2025-26 notes 35% of rural households lack healthcare within 5 km.

new.s: The 'Hindu method of tribal absorption' is associated with:
new.x: N.K. Bose described the Hindu method of tribal absorption; Surajit Sinha gave the tribe-caste continuum.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of tribal society as against peasant society?
new.x: Market links and individual land mark peasant society; tribes are kinship-based, egalitarian and hold land and forest in common.

new.s: What share of India's Scheduled Tribe population lives in rural areas?
new.x: 89.97% of STs are rural; India has 705 ST groups.

new.s: Jan Breman's 'Footloose Labour', on circular migrants in casual informal jobs, was published in:
new.x: Breman's 'Footloose Labour' (1996) studied circular migrants in seasonal, casual and informal work.

new.s: How many Scheduled Tribe communities are there in Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: AP has 34 ST communities with 27.39 lakh STs (5.53%).

new.s: Among the old 13 districts, which was the least urbanised district of Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: Srikakulam (16.16%) was the least urbanised; Visakhapatnam (47.45%) and Krishna (40.81%) the most.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh:
1. Its urban share rose from 24.13% in 2001 to 29.47% in 2011.
2. Among its 28 districts, Polavaram is the most urbanised.
3. Its Scheduled Areas cover 3,512 villages.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; statement 2 is wrong because Polavaram (2.84%) is the least urbanised and Visakhapatnam the most.

new.s: Customs and marriage norms being absorbed early in life point to which cause of casteism?
new.x: Family and socialisation make people absorb caste customs and marriage norms early.

new.s: The 'honour killings paradox' refers to States that have:
o: Fewer inter-caste unions and fewer honour killings
More inter-caste unions and fewer honour killings
More inter-caste unions and more honour killings
new.x: In TN, Telangana, Maharashtra and Kerala, both inter-caste unions and honour killings are higher.

new.s: Haldwani, where a 'purification' ritual after Kharge's rally was attacked as untouchability, is in:
new.x: The Haldwani (Uttarakhand) 'purification' ritual was criticised as a form of untouchability.

new.s: Caste associations function in Indian politics mainly as:
new.x: Caste associations act as pressure groups, alongside caste-based voting.

new.s: The Bihar caste survey cited as a model for caste enumeration was held in:
new.x: The Bihar survey (2022-23) is cited as a model as Census 2027 returns caste enumeration.

new.s: After Karamchedu, independent Dalit Mahasabhas in Andhra Pradesh were led by:
o: Gurram Jashuva and Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu
Katti Padmarao and Manda Krishna Madiga
new.x: Katti Padmarao and Manda Krishna Madiga led the Dalit Mahasabhas after Dalits left the Congress and Communists.

new.s: Which Article of the Constitution guarantees access to shops and public places without caste discrimination?
new.x: Art. 15(2) covers access to shops and public places; Art. 17 abolishes untouchability and Art. 21 covers choice of spouse.

new.s: The helpline for complaints under the Atrocities Act is:
new.x: Helpline 14566 helps register FIRs under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

new.s: PM-DAKSH, a support measure for Scheduled Castes, provides:
new.x: PM-DAKSH is a skilling scheme; the Venture Capital Fund and Ambedkar Overseas Vidya Nidhi are separate measures.

new.s: The Satyashodhak Samaj was founded in 1873 by:
new.x: Jyotiba Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873 and wrote 'Gulamgiri'.

new.s: 'Gabbilam' (1941) was written by:
new.x: Gurram Jashuva, born at Vinukonda, Guntur, wrote 'Gabbilam' (1941), 'Firadausi' and 'Kristu Charitra'.

new.s: B.R. Ambedkar's 'Annihilation of Caste' was published in:
new.x: 'Annihilation of Caste' appeared in 1936; 1924 is the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Jyotiba Phule:
1. He was given the title 'Mahatma' in 1924.
2. He was born in Pune in 1827.
3. He started the first girls' school in 1848.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct; statement 1 is wrong because Phule got the 'Mahatma' title in 1888.

new.s: In Shakti Vahini v. Union of India (2018), khap interference in marriages of consenting adults was held to be:
o: Valid if approved by the gram sabha
new.x: The Supreme Court held khap interference illegal and laid down preventive, remedial and punitive measures.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a direction in Shakti Vahini v. Union of India (2018)?
o: Caste panchayats may settle marriages of consenting adults
new.x: Shakti Vahini declared khap interference illegal; it did not let caste panchayats settle such marriages.
